newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mostly down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mostly down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly down on Tuesday due to profit-taking following flat overnight performance on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active April 1997 contract ended at 21,540 yuan ($2,596) per tonne, losing 220 yuan. It opened at an intra-day high of 21,760 and hit a low of 21,500.
January rose 90 to 21,290, February was unchanged at 21,250, March fell 140 to 21,310, May 220 to 21,640, June 170 to 21,650 and July 200 to 21,700.
Combined volume rose to 71,440 tonnes from 45,890.
Copper opened little changed but profit-taking pushed the contracts down to, or near, their intra-day lows.
Traders said LME copper did not rise sharply last night as many Shanghai investors had expected, triggering profit-taking.
"Profit-taking dominated today's trading with many long position holders revising their optimistic assessments of the market," one trader said.
"A second reason was that many investors wanted to liquidate their positions and take a rest with the approach of the Chinese lunar new year holiday," he added.
"Investors will not build large positions in the short term with sentiment discouraged," a second trader said.
Analysts expect copper to move around 21,500 yuan in the next few days.
Aluminium ended mostly up. January rose 50 to 14,750 yuan per tonne, February was unchanged at 15,000, March gained 20 to 15,300 and April was up 100 at 15,600.
Combined volume fell to 1,980 tonnes from 2,090.
